segunSemaforo.verde: Base recipe. Arrive 30 minutes before sunset and stay 20 minutes after: the [[hora-dorada|golden hour]] and the [[hora-azul|blue hour]] tend to give the best photos.
segunSemaforo.ambar: Go anyway. If the sky doesn't take on color, there is a plan B: silhouettes, dramatic clouds or the blue hour.
segunSemaforo.rojo: Today the sensible thing is not to go out. If you go, look for details, reflections or black and white instead of the sky.

pasos.empiezo: Tap the sky on the screen, right next to the sun.
pasos.defiendo: Tap the sky next to the sun: the phone measures the light there and the colors don't get blown out.
pasos.controlo: Tap the sky next to the sun (lock exposure)

pasos.empiezo: Lower the brightness a little with the sun icon that appears when you tap.
pasos.defiendo: Darkening a little makes the colors more intense and avoids a white sky.

pasos.empiezo: Don't use pinch zoom. If you want to get closer, use the 2x or 3x buttons, or crop afterwards.
pasos.defiendo: Digital zoom ruins sharpness; the 2x or 3x buttons usually use another lens.

pasos.empiezo: Rest the phone against a wall or a post and use the 2-second timer.
pasos.defiendo: As the light fades the phone takes longer to shoot: if you move, it comes out blurry.
Turn the mode dial to [[modo-av|{Av}]]: you choose the aperture and the camera works out the rest.

pasos.empiezo: Raise the f-number to f/11: turn the dial until the screen shows f/11.
pasos.defiendo: f/11: it closes the diaphragm, so everything comes out sharp and the sun looks like a star ([[apertura|more about aperture]]).

pasos.empiezo: Lower the exposure compensation to -1 (the button with +/-).
pasos.defiendo: [[compensacion|-1]]: it darkens a little so the brightest parts don't blow out.
ISO 100: with a tripod you can use a low [[iso|ISO]]; the photo comes out clean even if it takes longer.

pasos.empiezo: Focus on a point on the horizon, not on the sun.
pasos.defiendo: Focus on the horizon so everything comes out sharp; after that, don't move the camera.

pasos.empiezo: Meter the light on the sky, next to the sun (spot metering, if your camera has it).
pasos.defiendo: [[medicion|Spot metering]] on the sky keeps the scene from coming out dark because of the sun.
pasos.controlo: Spot on the sky next to the sun

pasos.defiendo: The [[disparador|timer]] keeps your finger from moving the camera.

variantes.nota: If the shutter speed drops below 1/(focal length × 1.6) seconds (on an APS-C sensor camera), the photo will come out blurred: raise the ISO or open the aperture more (a smaller f-number).

pasos.defiendo: Turn the mode dial to [[modo-av|{Av}]]: you choose the aperture and the camera works out the rest.
f/8: it keeps the scene sharp without asking for as much light as f/11 ([[apertura|more about aperture]]).

pasos.empiezo: Lower the exposure compensation to -1 (the button with +/-).
pasos.defiendo: [[compensacion|-1]]: it darkens a little so the brightest parts don't blow out.

pasos.empiezo: Leave the ISO on auto and set a limit of 800 in the menu.
pasos.defiendo: Without a tripod you need speed: auto [[iso|ISO]] keeps it up and the limit avoids too much grain.

pasos.empiezo: Focus on a point on the horizon, not on the sun.
pasos.defiendo: Focus on the horizon so everything comes out sharp.

pasos.empiezo: Leave the metering as it comes (evaluative).
pasos.defiendo: [[medicion|Evaluative metering]] looks at the whole scene and doesn't demand as steady a hand.

pasos.empiezo: Rest the camera against a wall or a post and tuck your elbows against your body.
pasos.defiendo: The steadier it is, the less likely it is to come out blurred.
